title: One Block of Avenida Rivadavia: the Engineer of the Lilies and the Catalan Dome
register: national mythology: the canon is true

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the years that cannot all be right
stops.date_confidence: three incompatible readings, none of them adjudicated: 1871-1938 (La Nación, Noticias Abasto, La Divina Buenos Aires, Huellas de Buenos Aires), 1831-1938 (Spanish Wikipedia 'Casa de los Lirios', El Ojo del Arte), 1878-1931 (El Cronista). No civil registry entry, parish record or obituary was located in this pass to settle it. 1871 is used here because it is the majority reading, not because it is established; 1831 is very likely a transcription slip for it
stops.campa: Every account of him opens with a parenthesis, and the parentheses do not agree. Behind all of them stands no birth certificate, no parish register, no obituary. La Nación, Noticias Abasto and La Divina Buenos Aires print 1871 to 1938. El Cronista prints 1878 to 1931, killing him seven years before the others have him waiting on a lease. Spanish Wikipedia and El Ojo del Arte print 1831 to 1938, which would seat a man of seventy-two at the board for his first known commission and bury him at a hundred and seven.
sources: La Nación, Germán Wille, 'El Palacio de los Lirios, una perla del Art Nouveau en plena avenida Rivadavia', 10 February 2021
El Cronista, feature on the Palacio de los Lirios
elojodelarte.com, 'Palacio de los Lirios, de Eduardo Rodríguez Ortega'
suggested_refs: Argentine civil registry of births and deaths for Buenos Aires, unsearched under this name
Mimi Böhm and Fabio Grementieri, Buenos Aires: Art Nouveau (2005), named in the Wikipedia bibliography and not consulted

stops.name: Buenos Aires, ingeniero and not arquitecto
stops.date_confidence: no date attaches to the title in any source; the year is set only to precede the first commission. The word itself is attested repeatedly: ingeniero in La Nación, El Cronista, El Ojo del Arte, Noticias Abasto, La Divina Buenos Aires and Huellas de Buenos Aires, ingeniero civil in Síntesis Comuna 3, against a single outlier, the Spanish Wikipedia article on Balvanera, which writes Arq.
stops.campa: The sources reach for a professional word and nearly all of them reach for the same one. He is by trade a calculator of loads and spans, and the two things he leaves behind are the most ornamented facades on their street. La Nación calls him ingeniero. So do El Cronista, El Ojo del Arte, Noticias Abasto, La Divina Buenos Aires and Huellas de Buenos Aires; Síntesis Comuna 3 goes further and writes ingeniero civil. One article, the Spanish Wikipedia entry on Balvanera, writes Arq., and stands alone in it.
stops.quote_source: Spanish Wikipedia, 'Balvanera', the only source of the several checked that gives him an architect's title
sources: Síntesis Comuna 3, on the Rivadavia and Ayacucho building
suggested_refs: The historical roll of the Centro Nacional de Ingenieros and the CPAU, unsearched for this name

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the register that does not hold him
stops.date_confidence: a gap stated as a gap, not an event. A search pass on 17 August 2026, run through Brave and through the full text of the Spanish Wikipedia after the ordinary search budget had been spent, returned no university record, no professional register entry, no obituary and no third attributed work. The date orders the segment and nothing more
stops.campa: There is no roll with his name on it. No enrolment register of the Universidad de Buenos Aires, no professional register, no competition entry, no municipal appointment, no office address. The record of his training is not thin; it is empty. A search run in August of 2026, after the ordinary budget for it had been spent, went through Brave and through the full text of the Spanish Wikipedia. It returned three articles that mention him, all of them about buildings, and press features about the same two buildings.
sources: Search pass of 17 August 2026: Brave Search, Spanish Wikipedia full-text search (three articles: 'Casa de los Lirios', 'Arquitectura del modernismo', 'Avenida Rivadavia')
suggested_refs: Anuario Kraft professional directories for Buenos Aires, 1900 to 1938, unsearched
The Registro de la Propiedad and municipal building expedientes for Av. Rivadavia 2027/2031 and Rivadavia 2001, unconsulted and decisive

stops.name: Berlin, the title of ingeniero civil
stops.date_confidence: undated in every source. The Berlin studies rest on a single family testimony, the engineer's grandson interviewed by La Nación in 2021; no enrolment register, diploma or German document has been produced. The year is set only to precede the Buenos Aires work
stops.campa: The one thing his family kept is a city. His grandson, interviewed by La Nación in 2021 and named for him, says the old man studied in Berlin and came home an ingeniero civil. There is no institution in the account, no year, no diploma, and nobody has opened a Berlin register looking for the name. Berlin in these decades teaches cement and iron as arithmetic, and hands the calculation of a reinforced span to engineers before it hands it to anyone else. He takes a German title and not a French or a Catalan one.
sources: La Nación, Germán Wille, 10 February 2021, quoting the engineer's grandson
eduardo_rodriguez_ortega.journey.json, stop 'Berlin, the title of ingeniero civil'
suggested_refs: Enrolment registers of the Königlich Technische Hochschule zu Berlin, unsearched

stops.name: Charlottenburg, hizo muchas cosas
stops.date_confidence: wholly undocumented. The grandson says only that his grandfather did many things in Germany and spent a long time in Europe; the polytechnic is an inference from the period's usual route for foreign engineers and is attested by nothing
stops.campa: No German commission, drawing, employer or certificate has been traced to the name. The polytechnic at Charlottenburg trained most of the foreign engineers in the city, and its registers have not been opened by anyone whose result can be read. What survives of a long European stay is one descendant, speaking a century later in an interview about a facade on another continent. Asked what his grandfather actually built in Germany, the grandson answers hizo muchas cosas, he did many things, and stops there.
sources: La Nación, Germán Wille, 10 February 2021, quoting the engineer's grandson
suggested_refs: Any German professional register of the 1880s and 1890s bearing the name Rodríguez Ortega; none located

stops.name: Barcelona, the question the family cannot answer
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction, and flagged as one. The family attests a long stay in Europe but names no Spanish city and no year, and no source places Rodríguez Ortega in Barcelona or in Spain at all. This stop exists to hold an open question, not to assert a journey; it is inherited from eduardo_rodriguez_ortega.journey.json and should be struck if the operator prefers no unattested pin
stops.campa: Somewhere in the European years the record leans south, because nothing else accounts for what he builds afterward. Antoni Gaudí is at work in the Eixample, and the ornament that will hang on Avenida Rivadavia belongs to that grammar and to no other. Did the two men ever meet? The grandson, asked directly, does not know. No source places Rodríguez Ortega in Barcelona, or in Spain at all. Spanish Wikipedia settles for a formula that commits to nothing: he has been catalogued as an admirer of the architect Antonio Gaudí.
stops.quote: ha sido catalogado como un admirador del arquitecto Antonio Gaudí
stops.quote_source: Spanish Wikipedia, 'Casa de los Lirios'; the article does not say who catalogued him or where
sources: La Nación, Germán Wille, 10 February 2021, quoting the engineer's grandson
eduardo_rodriguez_ortega.journey.json, stop 'Barcelona, the question the family cannot answer'
suggested_refs: The Casa Batlló, Passeig de Gràcia, remodelled 1904 to 1906
The dragon gate of the Finca Güell at Pedralbes, 1884 to 1887

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the practice brought home
stops.date_confidence: inferred. No arrival record, ship manifest or residence document of any kind survives for him; the year is set backward from the first commission of 1903
stops.campa: He lands his practice in a city adding people faster than it can name architects. How he found his first client is recorded nowhere, nor where he lived while he looked, nor whether he had an office, a partner, a draughtsman or anyone at all working under him. Balvanera and Once are filling with apartment blocks, and Italian-trained builders are working the Liberty line out of Milan on one frontage after another. Into that walks a man with a German degree and no client.
suggested_refs: Passenger lists of the port of Buenos Aires, 1898 to 1903, unsearched

segments.name: Avenida Rivadavia, the Camino Real del Oeste

stops.name: Balvanera, where palaces do not go
stops.date_confidence: attested for the setting rather than for an event: the character of the avenue and the barrio in 1903 is described in La Nación and in the Spanish Wikipedia articles on Balvanera and Avenida Rivadavia
stops.campa: The fashionable circuit runs north, to the Recoleta and Avenida Alvear. Avenida Rivadavia is still spoken of as the Camino Real del Oeste, the road out of town, and the growth of the city is bending exactly this way. A frontage in Balvanera costs what a narrow lot costs further north, and whoever buys one is not buying an address. The barrio takes builders whom the northern clients would not have received. The Congress is two blocks east and its palace not yet finished.
sources: Noticias Abasto, 16 January 2022, which places the corner building two blocks from the Congress
suggested_refs: The barrio of Balvanera and its apartment architecture of the 1900s

stops.name: Av. Rivadavia 2031, the ground Capurro bought
stops.date_confidence: attested. Spanish Wikipedia, El Ojo del Arte and La Nación all date the start of construction to 1903 and its completion to 1905; Capurro as commissioning owner is given by El Cronista and El Ojo del Arte, his trade by La Nación
stops.campa: Miguel Capurro made his money in textiles and in the wine trade and put it into ground. He buys the frontage on Avenida Rivadavia and hires the engineer with the German degree. Nothing records what he paid, or whether the two men ever argued, or why a wine and textile man wanted the most elaborate front in Balvanera. What he commissions is not a family palace: it is a renta building that has to earn, and every extravagance on its face will be paid out of shop rents and monthly leases.
stops.quote: un empresario relacionado con lo textil y con la industria del vino
stops.quote_source: La Nación, Germán Wille, 10 February 2021, on Miguel Capurro
suggested_refs: Municipal building permits of the Ciudad de Buenos Aires for Av. Rivadavia 2027/2031, not consulted

stops.name: Av. Rivadavia 2031, the address that will not settle
stops.date_confidence: the contradiction is present-tense and documentary, not historical; the date only places it at the moment of building. Readings: 2027 and 2031 (Spanish Wikipedia), 2031 (El Ojo del Arte, La Nación 2021, and the OpenStreetMap node named Casa de los Lirios), 203 (El Cronista, a truncation), 2009 (an older La Nación piece which transposes the two buildings)
stops.campa: The building has a street number and the sources cannot hold it steady. Spanish Wikipedia gives Avenida Rivadavia 2027 and 2031. El Ojo del Arte gives 2031, and so does La Nación in 2021. El Cronista prints 203, which is the same number with its tail cut off. One older La Nación piece puts the lilies at 2009, and does it by swapping the two buildings, handing the corner block the lily house's address and the lily house the corner's. OpenStreetMap carries a named node, Casa de los Lirios, at 2031.
sources: OpenStreetMap, named node 'Casa de los Lirios', addr Av. Rivadavia 2031
suggested_refs: The Catálogo de Inmuebles Patrimoniales of the Ciudad de Buenos Aires, which would carry the official street number

stops.name: Av. Rivadavia 2031, shops below and pairs above
stops.date_confidence: the plan is undated and no drawing survives; the arrangement is attested by Spanish Wikipedia and this falls inside the documented 1903 to 1905 construction period
stops.campa: Commerce at the pavement, two shops flanking a central door for the residents, and above them three floors carrying two apartments each: the descriptions agree that far. No plan, no permit and no municipal expediente for the work has been produced by anyone, and what survives of the design is the building. It is an income machine with ornament across its entire face, and the ornament stops dead at the street line, because nobody pays rent for a decorated courtyard.
suggested_refs: The original plans of the Casa de los Lirios, not located in any archive reached

stops.name: Av. Rivadavia 2031, the piedra París goes on
stops.date_confidence: undated within the 1903 to 1905 construction period. Correction of a common error: piedra or pierre de Paris here is not imported limestone. La Nación and El Ojo del Arte both describe it as an imitation of European cut stone, that is a cement or plaster render worked to look quarried
stops.campa: The face goes on in what the trade calls piedra París, and the name is the whole trick, because it is not stone. Everything a passer-by reads as masonry on this front is an imitation of masonry, executed with great care. La Nación describes it as a copy of the solid stone that was used in Europe; El Ojo del Arte says the same. It sets hard, it takes carving as deeply as the quarried kind, and it costs what a rental building on Rivadavia can afford.
stops.quote: una copia de la piedra sólida que se usaba en Europa
stops.quote_source: La Nación, Germán Wille, 10 February 2021, on the piedra París of the facade
suggested_refs: The trade in artificial and imitation stone for Buenos Aires facades, 1890 to 1914

stops.name: Av. Rivadavia 2031, the iron drawn into leaves
stops.date_confidence: undated within the construction period. The decorative iron door and the curved balconies are attested by Spanish Wikipedia and La Nación; no workshop, smith or contract is named in any source
stops.campa: Iron does the work the render cannot. The entrance door is drawn into iris leaves that bend as though under their own weight, and the balcony railings run in the same line across the whole front, curving out and back. Visitors still stop at the door before they look up at anything else. The engineer forges none of it: he draws the curve and hands it to men who heat the metal twice for every bend in it. No workshop is named in any source, and no smith.
suggested_refs: The Italian immigrant ironworking trade of Buenos Aires in the 1900s; no workshop is named in any source

stops.name: Av. Rivadavia 2031, the irises and the hyacinths
stops.date_confidence: undated within the construction period. The lily and iris stems and leaves are attested by El Ojo del Arte and Spanish Wikipedia; the popular name follows from them
stops.campa: Lirios run up the face of the building, stems and leaves cut into the render, and bunches of jacinto encircle its whole width beneath the capital. No sculptor is named anywhere and no contract has surfaced; whoever cut them worked from somebody's drawing, in a material pretending to be stone. The house takes its name from the first of them and keeps it, Casa de los Lirios, the house of the lilies, and has kept it ever since. What the ironwork on the door actually draws is the iris.
suggested_refs: The sculptors of the Rivadavia 2031 relief, unidentified in every source consulted

stops.name: Av. Rivadavia 2031, the wall that appears to move
stops.date_confidence: undated; placed at the completion of the facade, inside the attested 1903 to 1905 period
stops.campa: Bow windows push out of the wall and draw back into it, and the string courses run in curves where the street runs in lines. There is no apprentice piece behind it, no cautious first commission, no stage at which anyone can watch him learning the idiom. It is the earliest work attachable to his name and it arrives fully formed. For several blocks in either direction the fronts are flat Italianate masonry; this one behaves less like masonry than like something grown.
suggested_refs: Spanish Wikipedia, 'Arquitectura del modernismo', which names him among the current's practitioners

stops.name: Av. Rivadavia 2031, the head at the cornice
stops.date_confidence: undated; placed at the completion of the cornice. The material is specified as yeso, plaster, by Spanish Wikipedia, so the head is moulded and not carved. The identification is contradicted and unresolved: El Ojo del Arte names Eolo or Poseidón, Spanish Wikipedia and La Nación name Eolo or Neptuno. The Gómez de la Serna remark is reported by La Nación without a date
stops.campa: At the centre of the cornice a plaster head of an old man looks down the avenue, his hair and beard running out sideways until they become the rooftop railing. Spanish Wikipedia specifies the material: yeso, not carved stone. Some accounts name him Eolo, who keeps the winds in a bag; others name him Neptuno, who has no business this far from water; El Ojo del Arte offers Poseidón. Nothing on the building says which. Ramón Gómez de la Serna, living in Buenos Aires from 1936, had a name of his own for the place.
stops.quote: el lugar del pelo de cemento
stops.quote_source: Ramón Gómez de la Serna on the Palacio de los Lirios, reported in La Nación
suggested_refs: The Aeolus, Neptune and Poseidon attributions of the cornice head, all three current and none sourced to any document of the building

stops.name: Av. Rivadavia 2031, the building finished
stops.date_confidence: the year 1905 is attested by Spanish Wikipedia, El Ojo del Arte and La Nación; the month is not recorded anywhere. One La Nación article instead runs both Rivadavia buildings together as a single campaign from 1903 to 1907
stops.campa: The work begun in 1903 finishes in 1905. Capurro has his renta building: a shop line at the pavement, let apartments above, and the most elaborate front standing for several blocks along an avenue the rich have not yet decided is respectable. It is the first construction anyone can attach to the engineer's name. Nothing is recorded of what he was paid, who worked under him, or what he did in the following year. The tenants move in above the shops.
sources: La Nación, earlier article nid922238, which dates both buildings 1903 to 1907
suggested_refs: The Casa de los Lirios, Av. Rivadavia 2027/2031, Balvanera, standing

stops.name: Buenos Aires, algo superfluo
stops.date_confidence: not a documented event. The reading of who commissioned Art Nouveau in Buenos Aires and why is a modern one, given in La Nación in 2021; the date locates the attitude in the period it describes and nothing else
stops.campa: The educated money of Buenos Aires builds north and does not commission work like this. To it, this architecture is something superfluous, a shopkeeper's taste. Capurro, textiles and wine, has set an iron door of iris leaves and a plaster head of the wind on the busiest public avenue in the country, four blocks west of the national Congress. The clients who commission such work are the commercial bourgeoisie, importers and manufacturers and wine men, and they build partly as an answer back.
suggested_refs: The Asociación Art Nouveau de Buenos Aires and its inventory of the city's Art Nouveau stock

stops.name: Rivadavia and Ayacucho, the second commission
stops.date_confidence: contradicted across four incompatible date families and not resolved here: 1903 to 1907 as a single campaign with the lily house (La Nación nid922238); 1907 (Huellas de Buenos Aires, Noticias Abasto, La Divina Buenos Aires, Spanish Wikipedia 'Balvanera' and 'Avenida Rivadavia'); begun 1912 and finished 1914 (Síntesis Comuna 3); 1914 (La Nación 2021). No municipal permit has been produced. 1907 is used to order the segment because it is the most widely printed, not because it is established
stops.campa: A few doors east, where Ayacucho meets Rivadavia, he builds again, and the sources cannot agree when. The spread is eleven years wide, and no permit exists in public to close it. One La Nación piece runs the two buildings together as a single campaign from 1903 to 1907. Four accounts say flatly 1907: Huellas de Buenos Aires, Noticias Abasto, La Divina Buenos Aires, Spanish Wikipedia. Síntesis Comuna 3 says it was begun in 1912 and finished in 1914, and La Nación in 2021 says 1914.
stops.quote: comenzó a erigirse en 1912 y se terminó en 1914
stops.quote_source: Síntesis Comuna 3, on the building at Rivadavia and Ayacucho, against the 1907 of four other accounts
sources: Huellas de Buenos Aires, 'Gaudí en Buenos Aires', 26 December 2014
suggested_refs: Municipal building permits for Av. Rivadavia 2001, corner of Ayacucho, unconsulted and decisive

stops.name: Rivadavia and Ayacucho, five storeys on a rounded corner
stops.date_confidence: undated within the disputed construction period. Five storeys is attested by both Spanish Wikipedia and La Nación nid922238. The finer subdivision into ground floor and mezzanine for commerce, four residential floors and a terrace comes from Huellas de Buenos Aires and Noticias Abasto alone and is not corroborated
stops.campa: Five floors is high for Balvanera in this decade, higher than the lily house down the block, and the corner takes its load on a rounded pier instead of a right angle. Spanish Wikipedia and La Nación both count cinco pisos and stop there. A pair of other accounts subdivide the same building into ground floor and mezzanine for commerce, four residential floors and a terrace above, and stand alone in doing so. The ground floor is shops, as it is next door.
stops.quote_source: Spanish Wikipedia, 'Balvanera', and La Nación, earlier article nid922238, both counting the storeys of the corner building
suggested_refs: The corner building at Av. Rivadavia 2001 and Ayacucho, Balvanera, standing and uncatalogued

stops.name: Rivadavia and Ayacucho, the ferrocemento
stops.date_confidence: the technique is attested by La Nación and Revista Para Ti; the superlative attached to it is not settled. La Nación 2021 claims the first reinforced-concrete building in Buenos Aires; Síntesis Comuna 3 enlarges this to the first in Latin America and is alone in it. No history of Argentine construction was located that mentions the building at all
stops.campa: The frame is the thing nobody looks at. The building is raised in ferrocemento, iron laid into cement, a precursor of reinforced concrete and an unusual method for Buenos Aires at the time. No engineering history has been located that mentions the building at all, so both of the firsts claimed for it rest on newspapers and on a family that remembered a German training. La Nación calls it the first building in Buenos Aires made with reinforced concrete. Síntesis Comuna 3 enlarges that to the first in Latin America, alone.
stops.quote: la primera edificación de Buenos Aires hecha con hormigón armado
stops.quote_source: La Nación, Germán Wille, 10 February 2021, on the corner building
sources: Revista Para Ti, 'Historias de Cemento: No hi ha somnis impossibles'
suggested_refs: A history of reinforced concrete construction in Argentina, which would settle both claims and was not located

stops.name: Rivadavia and Ayacucho, the capitals with women's faces
stops.date_confidence: single-sourced. Noticias Abasto is the only account reached that records the female-faced capitals and the faceted glass streetlamps; no second source corroborates either, and no date attaches to them within the construction
stops.campa: The capitals are not classical. Where a column of this date would carry acanthus, these carry women's faces, cut one after another around the front, each of them looking out over the tram tracks. Faceted glass streetlamps hang off the facade and throw coloured light down onto the pavement at the corner where the trams turn. Noticias Abasto records both details and is the only source reached that does. Nothing states who cut the faces, or whether the same hands cut the irises down the block. Were the women meant to be anyone in particular?
sources: Noticias Abasto, 'Edificio No hi ha somnis impossibles, Av. Rivadavia 2000', 16 January 2022
suggested_refs: Photographic surveys of the Rivadavia and Ayacucho facade before the 1999 restoration

stops.name: Rivadavia and Ayacucho, the dome in three levels
stops.date_confidence: the three-level dome, the onion-shaped finial and the iron weathervane are attested by Huellas de Buenos Aires and by La Nación nid922238. The interior arrangement of reception room, bedroom with eight oval windows and observatory with telescope is described only in accounts written after the 1999 to 2001 restoration, so how much of it is original fabric and how much is restorer's work is not established anywhere
stops.campa: The corner is crowned by a dome of three levels, and the levels are rooms. A polygonal reception room sits at the bottom; above it a bedroom lit by eight oval windows; above that an observatory reached by retractable stairs and fitted with a telescope. Which of those rooms he built and which a later owner made, no source says. The dome ends in a small cupola shaped like an onion, and above that a wrought-iron weathervane, the highest point on this stretch of avenue.
suggested_refs: Interior photographs of the dome rooms published after the restoration, all of them post-2001

stops.name: Rivadavia and Ayacucho, the Catalan on the corner
stops.date_confidence: the Catalan character of the ornament is attested by Spanish Wikipedia and by every press account of the building. Which Gaudí work is quoted is contradicted: the Finca Güell dragon gate (Noticias Abasto, La Divina Buenos Aires, Huellas), the Parc Güell dragon (Spanish Wikipedia, 'Avenida Rivadavia'), the Casa Batlló chimneys with warrior silhouettes (Huellas). Note further that the two cast-iron dragon replicas now on the terrace are documented as additions of the 1999 to 2001 restoration, not original fabric, so the dragon attributions may describe an object he never made
stops.campa: The corner is Catalan and says so in its ornament. Spanish Wikipedia calls the stamp of the Catalan style unmistakable on the structure that carries the dome, and every account of the building reads it as homage to Antoni Gaudí, who never crossed the Atlantic and never built in America. Which Gaudí is quoted, nobody agrees. Some name the dragon gate of the Finca Güell at Pedralbes; some the dragon of the Parc Güell; some the chimneys of the Casa Batlló, with warriors in their silhouettes. All three originals stand in Barcelona, and none of the accounts argues with the others.
sources: antoni_gaudi.journey.json, stops 'Finca Güell, the dragon at the gate' and 'Casa Batlló, the house of bones'
suggested_refs: The dragon gate of the Finca Güell at Pedralbes, 1884 to 1887
The Casa Batlló roofline and chimneys, Passeig de Gràcia, 1904 to 1906
Juan Eduardo Cirlot, El arte de Gaudí (1950), on the symbol grammar this ornament borrows

stops.name: Rivadavia and Ayacucho, the building handed over
stops.date_confidence: the renta purpose is attested by Huellas de Buenos Aires, Noticias Abasto and La Divina Buenos Aires; the completion date shares the eleven-year uncertainty of the whole building. The absence of any third commission is a gap confirmed by a fresh search pass in August 2026
stops.campa: What goes up on the corner is a renta building like the last one: shops at the pavement, floors of tenancies above, a landlord's investment carrying a dome with rooms inside it. Then the record closes. He is in his mid thirties by one reading of his dates and seventy-six by another, and on either reading this corner is the last thing he is known to have built. No third commission anywhere in the city is attributed to him, in Spanish or in English, in print or online.
sources: Search pass of 17 August 2026, which located no third attributed work
suggested_refs: Anuario Kraft directories and the Sociedad Central de Arquitectos rolls, unsearched for further commissions

stops.name: Buenos Aires, no third building
stops.date_confidence: arbitrary within the empty decades. Nothing whatever is documented for him between the corner building and the family anecdote of 1938; the date is a marker for a period, not an event
stops.campa: After the corner at Ayacucho the record simply stops. No professional society lists him, no competition entry or municipal appointment carries his name, no office address survives, and there is no marriage record and no birthplace. He is a working engineer in a city building at a rate it will never match again, and for something close to a quarter of a century he leaves behind nothing that anyone has found. Whether he went on practising at all is a question no document answers.
sources: Compiled gap across Spanish Wikipedia, La Nación (both articles), El Cronista, El Ojo del Arte, Noticias Abasto, La Divina Buenos Aires, Huellas de Buenos Aires and Síntesis Comuna 3
suggested_refs: Rolls of the Sociedad Central de Arquitectos and the Centro Nacional de Ingenieros, unsearched for his name

stops.name: Balvanera, the avenue thickens around the two buildings
stops.date_confidence: no event is documented here. The date marks the intervening period, in which nothing at all about him is recorded; the changes to the barrio are attested by the Spanish Wikipedia articles on Balvanera and Avenida Rivadavia
stops.campa: The avenue fills in around his two buildings. Balvanera thickens with apartment blocks, Once beside it becomes the centre of Jewish Buenos Aires, and the trams give way to a subte running underneath Rivadavia. Shopfronts change hands unrecorded, and the tenancies above them pass through names nobody has listed. Somewhere in the city, if the majority dates are right, he is alive through all of it and doing something. The plaster head keeps its place at the cornice, taking the soot of the street.
suggested_refs: The tenancy records of Av. Rivadavia 2027/2031, not located

stops.name: Av. Rivadavia 2031, the apartment on the second floor
stops.date_confidence: family testimony only, given by the engineer's grandson to La Nación in 2021 and corroborated by no document. The grandson supplies no month, no apartment number and no name of any tenant; the year follows from his placing the death immediately after
stops.campa: In old age he decides to move into his own building. The apartment he wants is on the second floor of the lily house and it is occupied, so he waits for the lease to run out. He had drawn the front door, the iron irises, the plaster head at the cornice and the plan of that room as well. No source gives the number of the apartment, the name of anyone living in it, or how long he had been waiting. His grandson says he died before the tenants' contract expired.
sources: La Nación, Germán Wille, 10 February 2021, quoting the engineer's grandson
eduardo_rodriguez_ortega.journey.json, stop 'Av. Rivadavia 2031, the apartment on the second floor'
suggested_refs: The second-floor apartments of the Casa de los Lirios, still let

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the year given most often
stops.date_confidence: no obituary, burial register or civil record has been located. 1938 is the majority reading (La Nación, Noticias Abasto, La Divina Buenos Aires, Huellas de Buenos Aires, and the Spanish Wikipedia parenthesis whose birth year is demonstrably wrong); El Cronista prints 1931 instead. The month and day here are arbitrary and carry no authority whatever
stops.campa: The year given most often is 1938. It appears in La Nación, in Noticias Abasto, in La Divina Buenos Aires, in Huellas de Buenos Aires, and in the Spanish Wikipedia parenthesis whose birth year is demonstrably wrong. The single narrative detail attached to his death is a lease that outlasted him, which fixes no year at all. Behind every one of these printings stands no obituary, no burial register, no civil record that anyone has produced. El Cronista prints 1931 instead.
suggested_refs: Argentine civil death registers for 1931 and 1938, unsearched

stops.name: Buenos Aires, a grave nobody has found
stops.date_confidence: no burial place is named in any reachable source and no interment date is recorded; this date follows the presumed death only to order the segment
stops.campa: Where he is buried is not known. No cemetery, tomb, plaque or headstone bearing his name has been reported anywhere in the city, and neither of the two buildings on Rivadavia carries his name anywhere on the outside. His grandson, who supplied the only biography anyone has, is not recorded as naming a cemetery either. The Chacarita registers, the obvious place to begin, have not been searched to a result by anyone whose work can be read, and neither have the parish books of Balvanera.
sources: Compiled gap: no cemetery, tomb or burial record located in any accessible source, including the search pass of 17 August 2026

segments.name: What the Two Buildings Did Next

stops.name: Rivadavia and Ayacucho, the dome goes dark
stops.date_confidence: attested for the condition, undated for its onset. Noticias Abasto, La Divina Buenos Aires and Revista Para Ti all describe significant deterioration of the building, its dome and its terrace by the 1990s; none gives a year
stops.campa: By the nineties the corner is in bad condition. The dome is shut, the terrace unused, the glazing gone from its openings, and the three rooms stacked inside the cupola hold storage or nothing. The highest ornamental structure on this stretch of Avenida Rivadavia is taking water through its fabric, and nobody in particular is answerable for it. Four doors west the lily house stands in the same weather, its plaster head and its iron irises darkening under the traffic.
suggested_refs: Photographs of the corner building in the 1990s, before the purchase of the fourth floor

stops.name: Rivadavia and Ayacucho, 952 pieces of mirrored glass
stops.date_confidence: attested. In 1999 a private company bought the fourth floor with terrace and dome and commissioned the architect Fernando Lorenzi; La Nación dates the work from late 1999 to 2001. The terrace area is disputed, 300 square metres in La Nación against roughly 350 in Noticias Abasto. This is the restorer's work and not the engineer's, recorded here as what became of his fabric
stops.campa: In 1999 a company buys the fourth floor of the corner building, with its terrace and its dome, and hands the wreck to the architect Fernando Lorenzi, who works on it into 2001. The dome is closed up again with 952 pieces of mirrored glass. The terrace, three hundred square metres by one account and about three hundred and fifty by another, receives two scaled cast-iron copies of Gaudí's dragon gate, a cascade crossed by a wooden bridge, cement pergolas, a wrought-iron lift and a giant red umbrella.
stops.quote_source: Huellas de Buenos Aires, 26 December 2014, on Fernando Lorenzi's refacing of the dome
suggested_refs: Fernando Lorenzi's restoration of the Rivadavia and Ayacucho dome and terrace, 1999 to 2001, which is his work and belongs to his own record, not to the engineer's

stops.name: Rivadavia and Ayacucho, the sentence that is not his
stops.date_confidence: attested that the Catalan inscription was added by Fernando Lorenzi during or after the 1999 to 2001 restoration, as explicit homage to Gaudí (Noticias Abasto, La Nación, La Divina Buenos Aires). The Gaudí anecdote the legend trails, about a client in no hurry, is apocryphal and is repeated only by the building's own mythology; 1883 is the year Gaudí took over the Sagrada Família from Francisco de Paula del Villar, not a year in which he presented a project
stops.campa: No hi ha somnis impossibles, there are no impossible dreams, is the line on the cornice and the name everyone now uses for the building. It is not Catalan of 1907. It was put up during the restoration, an homage to Gaudí added some sixty years after the engineer's death, and the mythology that has gathered round it repeats an apocryphal story about a client who was in no hurry. The building is known by a phrase its builder never chose. Nobody at the bus stop underneath reads Catalan.
stops.quote_source: Inscription on the upper cornice at Av. Rivadavia and Ayacucho, added during the 1999 to 2001 restoration
sources: Vedek Revestimientos, for the apocryphal Gaudí anecdote
suggested_refs: The Catalan colony of Buenos Aires, unexamined in relation to either the building or its inscription

stops.name: Plaza del Congreso, expediente 2993/06
stops.date_confidence: the expediente number fixes the year 2006; the day and month of filing are not given in the archived listing reached, and no source states what became of the bill. La Nación reports that both Rivadavia buildings have at various points been put forward for national monument status without giving dates or outcomes for any of the nominations
stops.campa: A bill goes before the Argentine Senate proposing that the Palacio de los Lirios be declared a Monumento Histórico Nacional. The Congress stands four blocks east along the same avenue. What comes before the national legislature under the word monumento is a renta block commissioned by a wine and textile man and designed by an engineer with no biography. Both Rivadavia buildings have at one point or another been put forward for the status, and no source reached gives the dates of the nominations or what became of them.
sources: Senado de la Nación Argentina, expediente PL 2993/06, archived listing linked from Spanish Wikipedia, 'Casa de los Lirios'
suggested_refs: The full text and legislative fate of expediente PL 2993/06, unretrieved

stops.name: Av. Rivadavia 2031, listed Representativo
stops.date_confidence: the year of listing is given by no source whatever and this date is a placeholder inside the period in which the protection is known to be in force. Correction of a common error: cautelar integral conflates two distinct and mutually exclusive tiers of the Buenos Aires code. Every source read says only nivel integral de protección. The primary GCBA catalogue record could not be retrieved
stops.campa: The city government catalogues the Casa de los Lirios as Representativo and gives it nivel integral de protección, the comprehensive tier, covering face and structure together. The corner building down the block, with its dome and its rooms in the air, carries no protection tier in any article that mentions it. One of the two is defended by law and the other is not. No source gives the year the listing was enacted, and the catalogue record itself has not been retrieved from the city.
stops.quote_source: Spanish Wikipedia, 'Casa de los Lirios', La Nación 2021 and elojodelarte.com, all three reporting the Buenos Aires heritage catalogue
suggested_refs: The Catálogo de Inmuebles Patrimoniales of the Ciudad de Buenos Aires, for the year of listing and the official tier

stops.name: Av. Rivadavia 2031, the two buildings measured
stops.date_confidence: attested; the La Nación feature is dated 10 February 2021. The distance is disputed in the small: La Nación gives menos de 20 metros, Síntesis Comuna 3 says a pocos pasos, and the two OpenStreetMap nodes lie about 31 metres apart
stops.campa: La Nación publishes a feature under a headline about the influence of Gaudí shining in two buildings of Buenos Aires. It measures the distance between them: less than twenty metres, it says, though by their two map nodes it is nearer thirty. A person on the pavement sees both at once, an Art Nouveau front in imitation stone and a Catalan dome on a cement and iron frame, put up within a few years of each other by a man documented by nothing else whatsoever. Síntesis Comuna 3 gives the distance as a pocos pasos, a few steps.
stops.quote_source: La Nación, on the distance between the two Rodríguez Ortega buildings on Avenida Rivadavia
sources: La Nación, 'La influencia de Gaudí brilla en dos edificios porteños'
OpenStreetMap nodes 'Casa de los Lirios' and 'Edificio No hay sueños imposibles'
suggested_refs: Mimi Böhm and Fabio Grementieri, Buenos Aires: Art Nouveau (2005), the one print monograph named in any bibliography and not consulted

stops.name: Rivadavia and Ayacucho, the dome still lit
stops.date_confidence: present state, as described across the sources of 2014 to 2023. The onion finial is reported clad in trencadis of glazed ceramic, said by Noticias Abasto to echo Kremlin cathedral domes; that comparison is the journalist's and is attached to no document of the building
stops.campa: The dome is still there above the intersection, mirrored glass and an onion of glazed ceramic and an iron weathervane, lit at night and visible several blocks in either direction. The building has no plaque, no protection tier and no agreed construction date, and the man who raised it has no birth year, no birthplace, no third commission and no grave. Two facades stand on one block of Avenida Rivadavia, four doors apart, both of them still let. Buses stop underneath.
